From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): “The Messenger of God (God bless him and his family) built his mosque one brick thick. قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام: «ولقد رأي: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: “On the night of Badr I saw that every one of us slept, except the Messenger of God (God bless him and his family): he stood upright at the foot of a tree, praying and supplicating until morning.”
فنادى عتبة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله: Utba called out to the Messenger of God (God bless him and his family): O Muhammad, send out to us our equals from Quraysh… Then he said: “Rise, Ali; rise, Hamza; rise, Ubayda. Fight for your right, with which God sent your Prophet, for they have come with their falsehood to put out the light of God.”
خرج عتبة وشيبة ابنا ربيعة والوليد بن عتب: Utba and Shayba, the sons of Rabi'a, and al-Walid ibn Utba came out seeking single combat. Ubayda ibn al-Harith, Hamza and Ali went out to meet them: “Al-Walid fought the Commander of the Faithful, who gave him no respite before killing him.”
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله: «غضوا: The Messenger of God (God bless him and his family) said: “Lower your eyes, clench your teeth, and do not draw a sword until I give you leave.” Then he raised his hand to the sky and said: “O Lord, if this band perishes You will not be worshipped; and if You will that You not be worshipped, You will not be worshipped.”
﴿إذ تستغيثون ربكم فاستجاب لكم أني ممدكم: “When you appealed to your Lord for help, He answered you: ‘I will aid you with a thousand angels in a file.’”
«وهو يسلت العرق عن وجهه ويقول: هذا جبرئي: “Wiping the sweat from his face, he was saying: This is Gabriel, who has come to you with a thousand angels in a file.”
كان قتلى المشركين يوم بدر سبعين، يعد الش: The polytheists slain at Badr numbered seventy. Al-Shaykh al-Mufid counts among them: “That makes thirty-five men, besides those about whom there is disagreement or in whose killing others shared with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him); and they are more than half of the slain.”
ثم أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله كفا: Then the Messenger of God (God bless him and his family) took a handful of pebbles and threw it in the faces of Quraysh, saying: “May the faces be disfigured!” God sent winds that beat against the faces of Quraysh, and the rout followed.
﴿وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى﴾: “And you did not throw when you threw, rather, it was God who threw.”

نصوص القرآن الكريم بالرسم الإملائي. وكل: Qur'anic texts are given in standard spelling. Every text attributed to Nahj al-Balagha has been checked against the Subhi al-Salih edition, and the new texts on this page were matched letter by letter against their pages in the Madrasat al-Fiqaha library (lib.eshia.ir), after unifying the spelling and removing the vowel marks and the formulas of blessing and peace; the scenes taken from the Life of Ali (peace be upon him) had their texts checked there against their books. This page is an unofficial labour of love. No one's face is drawn in it: the Prophet (God bless him and his family) and the People of the Cloak (peace be upon them) have a white veil over the face and a golden disc behind the head, after the custom of miniatures, and everyone else is a featureless shadow.

هذه سيرة رسول الله محمد بن عبد الله صلى: This is the life of the Messenger of God, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah (God bless him and his family), as the Imami books tell it: al-Kafi; al-Irshad and Masar al-Shi'a by al-Shaykh al-Mufid; the Amali of al-Saduq and of al-Mufid; the Tafsir of Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi; and Nahj al-Balagha, in which Ali (peace be upon him) describes him with the eye of one who stayed by his side from childhood. He was born in the Year of the Elephant, was sent at the turn of forty, called his people for thirteen years in Mecca, then emigrated to Medina and stayed there ten. Scroll the page as the years go by; the counter at the top of the screen counts his age.
